text: Searching for internet, you want the best: maximum speed, zero lag. It's the obvious choice for a seamless experience. Faster must be better, right?
You pick the ultra-fast plan. But wait – it has a surprisingly low data cap. The fastest internet often gives you the least data. This feels backwards.
It seems like a trick. Why pay more for speed if you can't use it? You expect premium service to offer both speed and unlimited data.
Here's the system. Fast users need bursts of speed, not constant heavy data. Capping their usage frees up network capacity for everyone.
The cost? You're paying for potential speed, often used briefly. The cap manages the shared network efficiently, optimizing for all.
Now you understand: data caps balance network load. They ensure consistent high speeds, preventing a few heavy users from monopolizing bandwidth.
